requirement.summary: CUS017 Daily Top GC Earners Report — GC member filter not working, shows non-member checks
requirement.description:
Background

CUS017 Daily Top GC Earners Report should only list checks related to GC members.

After TiDB compatibility changes, the GC member filter no longer works correctly: checks without a GC member still appear in the report.

Root cause (fixed in r70368):

- Member number is selected as IFNULL(ckei_member_number.ckei_value, 0) AS guest_no

- On TiDB / compatible environments, non-member checks get guest_no = '0' (not empty string)

- Old filter guest_no <> '' does not exclude '0', so non-member checks pass through

- Fix: change filter to guest_no <> '0'

Report file: Plugin/Pos/webroot/reports/daily_top_gc_earners/daily_top_gc_earners.rptdesign

Customer: shangrilagroup

Related: HERO-60152 (CUS016), HERO-60153 (CUS019)

Steps to Reproduce

- Prepare data for the same outlet / business day:

- At least one closed check with GC membership (membership_interface / member_number filled, points earned)

- At least one closed check without GC membership (no membership_interface member_number; guest_no effectively 0)

- Log in to Hero Report and open CUS017 Daily Top GC Earners Report

- Select the shop / outlet that has the above checks

- Select the business day of those checks

- Set No. Of Member (or leave default) and run the report

Expected Result

- Only GC member-related checks are listed

- Checks without GC member number (guest_no = 0) do not appear

- GC Number / Name / Tier show valid member values

Actual Result

- Non-GC-member checks also appear in the report

- Those rows may show GC Number as 0 / blank member name / blank tier

- Ranking / totals can be skewed by non-member checks

Suggested Verification (QA)

- On build with r70368 (or later), re-run the same parameters

- Confirm non-member checks are excluded and only GC earners remain

- Spot-check member number / name / points against POS check extra infos

requirement.summary: Report - TMS037 Master Pre-Race Booking List with Contact Information - Add Syndicate Owner Indicator field
requirement.description:
User Story

As a TMS report user, I want the Syndicate Owner Indicator field displayed in the TMS037 Master Pre-Race Booking List with Contact Information report so that I can identify the syndicate owner indicator for each reservation directly in the report without cross-referencing other systems.

Current Behavior

The Syndicate Owner Indicator field exists on the TMS reservation record (ref. HERO-64070, HERO-67705) but is not shown in the TMS037 Master Pre-Race Booking List with Contact Information report. The report currently displays the Syndicate Owner field without its indicator.

Expected Behavior

The TMS037 Master Pre-Race Booking List with Contact Information report should display a new "Syndicate Owner Indicator" column placed immediately to the LEFT of the existing "Syndicate Owner" column. The indicator should appear in all output formats — printed copy, on-screen preview, and file export. When a reservation has no indicator value (e.g., older or legacy reservations), the cell should be left blank. The field is display-only; no sorting, grouping, or filtering behaviour is required. All users who can access the report should see the indicator — no role restrictions.

Acceptance Criteria

Display Syndicate Owner Indicator column

- Given the user opens the TMS037 Master Pre-Race Booking List with Contact Information report

- When the report is generated

- Then a new "Syndicate Owner Indicator" column is displayed immediately to the left of the "Syndicate Owner" column

- And the indicator value is populated from the reservation's syndicate owner indicator data (hkjc_resv_members: rmem_syndicate_owner_indicator)

Show indicator in all output formats

- Given the TMS037 report contains reservations with syndicate owner indicator values

- When the report is viewed on screen, printed, or exported to a file

- Then the Syndicate Owner Indicator column appears in all three output formats (on-screen preview, printed copy, and file export)

- But if a reservation has no syndicate owner indicator value (e.g., older or legacy reservations), the cell for that reservation is left blank in all three output formats

Display-only field with no role restrictions

- Given a user has access to the TMS037 report

- When the user views the report and interacts with the Syndicate Owner Indicator column

- Then the field is display-only with no sorting, grouping, or filtering behaviour applied

- And the column is visible to all such users with no role-based restrictions

Supporting Evidence

- DB field: hkjc_resv_members: rmem_syndicate_owner_indicator (confirmed with TMS team)

- Related tickets: HERO-64070, HERO-67705 (Syndicate Owner Indicator added to TMS reservation record)

- Scope: This ticket covers only TMS037; the other 9 reports (TMS009, TMS015, TMS016, TMS020, TMS022, TMS024, TMS025, TMS035, TMS039) are handled in separate tickets.

Requested Timeline

Aligned with Priority: Medium

Preferred Quarter: Not specified

Target Version: Not specified

Notes: No explicit deadline provided by requester.

Original Description (preserved by INF Prod. Studio)

Background

Syndicate Owner Indicator field is added to TMS reservation record (ref. HERO-64070, HERO-67705). It is also needed to show in several reports.

Requirement

In the 10 reports below,

| TMS009 Special Booking List (By Outlet)

| TMS015 Pre-Race Booking List

| TMS016 Post-Race Booking List

| TMS020 Waiting List Report

| TMS022 Master Pre-Race Booking List

| TMS024 Waiting List Extraction

| TMS025 Unsuccessful Waiting List Report (By Outlet)

| TMS035 Waiting List Report (Owner Box)

| TMS037 Master Pre-Race Booking List with Contact Information

| TMS039 Override Date Limitation for Advance Booking

To add "Syndicate Owner Indicator" field on the LEFT of "Syndicate Owner” field.

requirement.summary: POS044 Audit Control Listing Report — wrong previous-day date on UTC HQ; optimize loading performance
requirement.description:
Summary / Background

- Report: POS044 — Audit Control Listing Report

- Design: Plugin/Pos/webroot/reports/audit_control_listing/audit_control_listing.rptdesign (MySQL; SQL Server design aligned where applicable)

- This case covers two issues on the same report:

- Date / timezone — auto report “Previous Day” shows the wrong calendar date on UTC HQ.

- Loading performance — main audit-log SQL is slow / appears to hang on large HQ DBs.

Issue 1 — Auto report date incorrect (UTC HQ)

Problem

Auto report email sent on a local morning date (e.g. 2025-01-14 ~06:06) with Date Type = Previous Day (last_bday), but the exported report header and row dates show two calendar days earlier (e.g. 2025-01-12) instead of local yesterday (2025-01-13). Server/DB is UTC.

Root Cause

current_bday / last_bday used bare MySQL CURRENT_DATE() (and BIRT today() for the header). On UTC HQ, local morning can still be the previous UTC calendar day, so “yesterday” is shifted by one extra day. iTimeOffset only shifted the UTC time window of that wrong calendar day; it did not choose the shop-local calendar day first.

Expected

- Previous Day = hotel local yesterday (via iTimeOffset).

- Header date matches the filtered local day.

Fix

- Local today SQL: DATE(DATE_ADD(NOW(), INTERVAL iTimeOffset MINUTE)); last day = that date − 1 day; then apply existing DATE_SUB(..., iTimeOffset) for alog_time UTC bounds.

- Header: localNow = BirtDateTime.addMinute(now, iTimeOffset − JVM offset), then format / addDay(..., -1) for last day.

- Preset must keep a correct iTimeOffset (e.g. UTC+8 → 480).

Issue 2 — Optimize loading performance

Problem

On large HQ databases (very large alog_logs / alog_log_infos), POS044 can run very slowly or appear to hang for a day + multi-outlet selection.

Root Cause

Optimizer often drives from out_outlets and reads alog_logs via outlet_slave (alog_olet_id, alog_slave_id), then applies alog_time as a residual filter (very low filtered). time_outlet (alog_time, alog_olet_id) is not used. Starting from alog_log_infos without a time-first hint makes this worse. Audit Log UI already forces time_outlet for similar queries.

Expected

- Time-first plan on alog_logs for dated listing queries.

- Report completes in a reasonable time on large volumes.

Fix

- Drive from alog_logs with FORCE INDEX (time_outlet), then join infos:

FROM alog_logs FORCE INDEX (time_outlet)
JOIN alog_log_infos ON alog_id = ainf_alog_id
...

- Same pattern as Audit Log LogsController / AuditLogGeneralComponent (forceIndex = 'time_outlet').

- SQL Server design: same join order from alog_logs (no MySQL FORCE INDEX).

References

- Report code: POS044

- Prior custom-report performance path: HERO-39055

- Screenshots on this ticket: auto mail 2025-01-14 vs report date 2025-01-12; parameter = Previous Day
requirement.release_notes:
Bug Fixing: [HERO-50978] POS044 Audit Control Listing Report - wrong Previous Day date on UTC HQ; one-day report cannot load
Descriptions:
This case fixes two problems in POS044 Audit Control Listing Report on Infrasys Cloud.
Date problem: When HQ runs on UTC time, an Auto Report with Date Type = Last day can show the wrong date. Example: the mail is sent on 2025-01-14 in the hotel local morning, but the report header and data show 2025-01-12 instead of local yesterday 2025-01-13. After this fix, Last day / Current Day follow the hotel local calendar, so the Auto Report date matches the hotel yesterday or today.
Performance problem: On a large HQ database, POS044 could not finish loading even when only one day one shop of data was selected. The report stayed running for a very long time and no result was returned. After this fix, a one-day POS044 report can load and show data.
No new report parameter is added. Existing Date Type (Current Day / Last Day / Specified) is unchanged.
Configuration / Parameter:
No new report parameter or system setting is added.
Date problem - how the wrong date appeared (before fix):
1. HQ database / report server time is UTC.
2. Hotel local time is ahead of UTC (for example UTC+8).
3. Set POS044 Auto Report Date Type = Previous Day.
4. Let Auto Report send in the hotel local morning, before UTC has crossed midnight (for example about 06:00 local time).
5. Open the attached POS044 Excel / PDF.
Result before fix: the report date is one extra day earlier than hotel local yesterday (mail date 2025-01-14, report date 2025-01-12).
Please confirm the shop time offset used by Auto Report is correct for the hotel (for example UTC+8). If the offset is 0, Last Day / Current Day may still follow UTC.
Performance part: no extra configuration is required. Use the same POS044 parameters as before (one day range and selected outlets).
Field Definition:
This case does not involve field definition.
Result / Sample:
After fix - date:
- Auto Report with Date Type = Previous Day shows hotel local yesterday in the report header and in the date column.
After fix - performance:
- Selecting one day of data, POS044 can load and return the listing. It no longer stays running for a whole day without result.
